column1: # PARAM.SFO - the title metadata table, as two independent open-source projects read and
# Columns: struct, field, offset, size, type, value, note
# read-from: pfd_sfo_tools  sfopatcher/src/sfo.{c,h}     C     READER + WRITER  [commit unrecorded]
#            ps5upload      engine/crates/ps5upload-pkg  Rust  reader + writer  [commit unrecorded]
# Both are public projects and the file paths are the reproduction path. Their commits were not
# The two sources, written years apart in different languages, agree on every field.
# The layout rows are measured, not cited. The C writer pads the key table so the whole file is
# a multiple of sixteen; no real file does. Eleven files were checked (three Prospero-generation
# packages, two Orbis-generation toolchain samples, six older-generation titles and saves): each
# pads the key table to a multiple of four and ends where its last value ends, and all eleven
# round-trip byte for byte. The refuted rule is kept as a row. No vendor binary was read to
# produce this table; real files confirm rows and never derive them.
# The version is recorded as the four bytes both sources write, `01 01 00 00` (1.1), not as an
# integer whose width a writer could get wrong.
# The structure is generation-independent. Which keys a title carries is content, not format,
# and is not in this table; Prospero-generation titles also carry `param.json`.
